🚨🇲🇽 <u>KEN SALAZAR MONETIZES INNUENDO AGAINST AMLO</u>

Former US ambassador Ken Salazar's memoir, out July 28, claims AMLO "feared what El Mayo could tell the US" — sourced entirely to an unnamed "businessman friend," with zero public evidence. Sheinbaum rejected the story flat from the mañanera. The same envoy she says misled the public on El Mayo's capture is now monetizing innuendo.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO AND BRAZIL REFUSE WASHINGTON'S NEW MONROE DOCTRINE</u>

The US launched its "Escudo de las Américas" anti-cartel coalition in Miami on March 7 — 11 Latin governments signed on, led by Rubio and Hegseth. Two refused: Mexico and Brazil, named by Contralínea as "the two main countries limiting absolute US hegemony over Latin America."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SLIM ACCUSES MEXICO'S TAX AGENCY OF A SHAKEDOWN</u>

Carlos Slim filed a corruption complaint accusing SAT tax officials of extortion — demanding payment to waive a 30% income tax on his companies' operations. Sheinbaum ordered an immediate investigation, promising dismissals and criminal charges if confirmed. This government is naming names inside its own tax agency.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>1 IN 5 GUNS SEIZED IN MEXICO CAME FROM SINALOA</u>

Harfuch reported today that Plan Sinaloa has seized 5,900 firearms and over a million cartridges since October 2024 — one of every five guns confiscated in all of Mexico. Barrett rifles, machine guns, grenade launchers: the hardware of a war fed by weapons that walk south across the US border.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>TOYOTA STAYS IN MEXICO — TARIFF DODGE MOVES ONE TRUCK LINE, NOT THE WORKFORCE</u>

Toyota is shifting Tacoma pickup production from Tijuana to a $3.6bn Texas plant to duck Trump's tariffs — but Mexico's Secretaría de Economía confirms the Guanajuato plant and its 2,800 jobs stay, phased out to 2030. The Tacoma is the second-most-exported vehicle made in Mexico: 24,558 units shipped January to May.

LATIN TIMES: Mexico's Finabien Card Emerges as Migrants' Shield Against U.S. Remittance Tax
July 5, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Rare fair coverage from a US outlet: Mexico built a state debit card so migrants can sidestep Trump's 1% remittance tax. $2.99 a transfer, free pickup at 53 consulates, 1,700 branches back home. 🇲🇽

A government building a public tool to protect its diaspora from a foreign tax — the story the networks won't touch. The card even pays 10% annual interest on savings.

• Finabien-to-Finabien counts as account-to-account, exempt from the Jan 1 excise tax
• the "Paisan@" card is issued through Financiera para el Bienestar

CBS NEWS: Toyota investing 3.6 billion in Texas plant, moving most Tacoma production from Mexico
July 7, 2026 | 🟡

📰 CBS runs Toyota's Texas move as a clean tariff win. Trump: "Toyota is moving from Mexico to the United States. Tariffs at work!" Not one line on the Mexican workers who build the Tacoma. 🇲🇽

Buried in the copy: Toyota keeps building Tacomas in Guanajuato and "encourages a quick resolution to USMCA." Coercion by 25% tariff, reported as market triumph. 💀

• "Tariffs at work!" — Trump, quoted, not scrutinized
• zero Mexican voices; no mention of the Guanajuato job impact

THE ECONOMIST: Mexico is placing an enormous bet on rail
July 6, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The Economist files Mexico's passenger-rail revival under "an enormous bet." A 7.7-billion-dollar program, 3,000 km of new electric track, ~490,000 jobs — framed as a gamble, not nation-building. 🇲🇽

Electric trains at up to 100 mph linking Mexico City to Guadalajara and Nuevo Laredo by 2030. When Washington poured trillions into highways, nobody called it a reckless wager.

🇲🇽📈 NUBANK COMMITS $4.2 BILLION TO MEXICO THROUGH 2030

Sheinbaum announced at Palacio Nacional that Nubank will invest $4.2 billion in Mexico between 2026 and 2030, after meeting founder David Vélez. The digital bank already counts nearly 14 million Mexican clients and plans to begin full banking operations in the country this year.

🇲🇽🌎 PAPANTLA'S LIME GROWERS SHIP THEIR FIRST HARVEST TO RUSSIA

Papantla, Veracruz just sent its first 21.4 tons of Persian lime to Russia, with 257.4 tons projected for the second half of 2026 — some 9,500 local citrus producers negotiating directly with foreign buyers and cutting out the intermediaries who long skimmed their harvests.
